claims.text: Machine-learning-driven optimization of stepwise thermo-mechanical processing can tailor coherent nanoprecipitate formation in refractory alloys.
Coherent nanoprecipitates can enable simultaneous improvement of strength and ductility in refractory alloys.
Traditionally processed refractory high-entropy alloys typically exhibit high strength with compromised ductility.
Traditionally processed conventional structural alloys typically exhibit high strength with compromised ductility.
Traditional processing typically produces single-phase or otherwise suboptimal precipitation structures.
Integrated processing-microstructure-property analytics can be used to optimize stepwise thermo-mechanical processing parameters.
The proposed benefit applies under ambient-temperature mechanical loading.
The proposed benefit applies under moderate-temperature mechanical loading typical of structural applications.
Stepwise processing forms controllable coherent nanoprecipitates within a continuous matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve localized stress concentrations associated with premature crack initiation.
The nanoprecipitates strengthen the alloy through precipitation hardening.
Relieving stress concentrations suppresses premature crack initiation and thereby improves tensile ductility.
The optimized route will increase both tensile strength and ductility relative to conventional processing routes.
The improvement should persist when testing conditions are similar to those used during optimization.
The effects may vary substantially with drastic composition changes or extreme service conditions.
The magnitude of strength and ductility improvement depends on alloy composition and processing parameters.
